Moderator: 
Ladies and gentlemen, good day and welcome to Central Bank of India Earnings Call for Q2 
FY2027 financial results. Please note all participant lines will be in the listen-only mode and 
there will be an opportunity for you to ask questions after the presentation concludes. Please 
note that this conference is being recorded. With that, I hand over the call to Mr. Siddharth 
Rajpurohit from Systematix Institutional Equities. Thank you and over to you. 
Siddharth Rajpurohit: 
Thank you Swapnil. Good morning everyone and welcome to Central Bank of India’s Q2 
FY2027 post results earnings call. From the management today we have Shri Kalyan Kumar, 
MD and CEO; Shri M. V. Murali Krishna, Executive Director; Shri Mahendra Dohare, 
Executive Director; Shri E. Ratan Kumar, Executive Director and Shri Vivek Kumar, Chief 
Financial Officer. I thank the management for giving us the opportunity and also congratulate 
the team for a very strong result. I am handing over now the call to MD, Shri Kalyan Kumar, 
for his opening remarks. Thank you. 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Thank you. My colleagues on the Board, Shri Murali Krishna Ji, Shri Dohare Ji, Shri Ratan 
Kumar Ji, my senior team present here, and all the analysts connected through VC. Good 
morning. First of all, I congratulate each one of you for this good Q2 2027 result. Your 
beloved bank, Central Bank of India’s total business has been actually grown by 20.54% to 
Rs.8,89,541 Crores and total domestic deposits increased by 14.41% to Rs.5,08,509 Crores. 
CASA deposit also stands at 44.65% of total deposits. Global advances increased by 29.83% 
to Rs.3,81,032 Crores, in which domestic advances stood at Rs.3,72,939 Crores, growth of 
27% year-on-year. We have opened GIFT City Branch on June 29, 2026, which contributed 
in overseas advance of Rs.8093 Crores and in this process we have given guidance for 
business growth 14% to 15% and we have achieved 20.54%, in deposit growth our guidance 
was 10% to 12% and we have achieved 14.41%, in advances growth our guidance was 14% 
to 16% and we have achieved 29.83%. CASA guidance was 48% plus or minus 1%. Here, 
due to obvious reason, due to FCNR(B) mobilization and other aspects, we could not meet 
the market guidance, and we closed at 44.65%, but towards RAM sector, Retail, Agriculture 
and MSME, as you know, Central Bank of India is having its 65% branches in rural and semi-
urban area. The RAM being our bread and butter for the organization, in which business grew 
by 21.11%. The individual sector-wise growth is also very good. In retail we reached to 
Rs.1,12,299 Crores with a growth of 24.49% year-on-year. In agriculture we reached to 
Rs.67,778 Crores with a growth of 19.92% and in MSME we reached to Rs.74,196 Crores, 
with a growth of 17.36% year-on-year basis. Actually, our guidance to market was RAM-to-
corporate credit ratio 65:35 plus or minus 5% and we have closed at 68:32 and that ratio 
actually also aligns with our market guidance which we have given. 
 
Towards our efficiency side also, business per employee has improved to Rs.25.26 Crores on 
year-on-year basis as against Rs.21.48 Crores for the quarter ended September 2025. In

profitability, year-on-year basis for September 2026 quarter, net profit for the quarter has 
increased by 21% to Rs.1469 Crores up from Rs.1213 Crores previous year. Operating profit 
for the quarter stood at Rs.2268 Crores from Rs.1786 Crores with a growth of 27%. Net 
interest income grew by 26.28% on year-on-year basis to Rs.4146 Crores in Q2 FY2027 as 
against Rs.3283 Crores in Q2 FY2026. Total income for Q2 FY2027 improved by 
approximately 15% and reached to Rs.11,737 Crores for Q2 FY2027. Cost-to-income ratio, 
though there is improvement but still it is on higher side it is 58.95% for Q2 FY2027 as 
against 62.42% Q2 FY2026. Cost-to-income ratio, we have given guidance for less than 56%, 
but here we could not match the guidance and closed at 58.95%. Major highlight, I would 
like to make that apart from stock cost that is 37.65%, there was 113-basis point improvement 
in other operating expenses year-on-year basis. Then as quarter-on-quarter also, it will give 
you comfort that quarter-on-quarter basis also, net profit grew by 11%, Rs.145 Crores in 
absolute terms to Rs.1469 Crores. Operating profit grew by 3.75% i.e. Rs.82 Crores in 
absolute terms to Rs.2268 Crores, net interest income grew by approximately 6% Rs.232 
Crores in absolute terms to Rs.4146 Crores, interest income grew by approximately 7% 
Rs.666 Crores in absolute terms to Rs.10,357 Crores, ROA improved by 3-basis points and 
stood at 1.03%. Here I would like to mention NIM, we have given guidance of above 3% and 
we have maintained at 3.01% and slippage ratio we have given guidance of less than 0.25% 
and it is 0.24%. 
 
Then regarding asset quality also our gross NPA stood at 2.39% that is also aligned with our 
guidance given to the market that it will be below 2.50%. Net NPA stood at 0.31%, also there 
is an improvement of 17-basis points and that is also in alliance with our guidance to the 
market. Provision coverage ratio stood at 97.16% and regarding slippage ratio, as I told, for 
the quarter, it is 1.24%, and it is well within our guidance of 1.25% on quarter-on-quarter 
basis. In that way, I can tell you on almost all the parameters of efficiency except cost-to-
income ratio, business-per-branch, and CD ratio, Bank is on track. I will highlight that 
liquidity coverage ratio improved to 156% and overall improvement in almost all the 
efficiency parameters and business numbers. Now, I really thank all our stakeholders, 
including our customers, regulators, governments, and all you beloved shareholders and 
stakeholders of this great organization, Central Bank of India. This was my initial remark, I 
conclude here. Now I am open to the questions. 
Moderator: 
Thank you so much Sir. Ladies and gentlemen, we will now begin with the question-and-
answer session. Anyone who wishes to ask a question may click on the raise hand icon from 
the participants tab on your screen. We will wait for a few minutes until the question queue 
assembles. We are taking our first question now. We have Mr. Ashok Ajmera of Ajcon 
Global. Mr. Ajmera, please unmute your microphone and go ahead with your question. Mr.

Choksey, please unmute your microphone and go ahead. 
Sushil Choksey: 
Congratulations to team Central Bank for excellent performance and sustainable guidance. 
Sir, I was looking at your business mix and can you throw some color, you guided on the CD 
ratio and the business mix for the second half, but can you see within RAM where are you 
seeing growth or it is per ticket average housing loans, car loans, which are growing or any 
other segment like gold loan, which is becoming a major force at Central Bank and you will 
have a very ambitious target, that is what I hear from the marketplace. 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Yes, thank you Mr. Choksey for asking this very good question. Regarding business mix, we 
have seen ratio of corporate and our RAM is 38:68. It aligns with actually our guidance given 
to 65:35 plus or minus 5% and growth of RAM sector was 21%. We reached the level of 
Rs.2,54,273 Crores and within which retail has grown by 24.49%, agriculture has grown by 
approximately 20%, MSME has grown by approximately 17%. So, good growth in all these 
three segments and rightly pointed out by you, this is going to continue because Central Bank 
of India is having its 65% branches in rural and semi urban area, which gives us this capability 
to support this important part of Indian economy. We will continue to grow with that, but 
rightly said by you, two latest growth engine in previous quarter, it was also there but here 
during last two days October 15, 2026 and October 16, 2026 we have mid-term strategy meet 
with our all general managers and regional heads, collectively we brainstormed regarding 
revisiting our strategies towards focus areas and how to grow and not only next half year but 
in longer term also. There we have important growth engine for gold loan side. We are going 
to open, customize 116 gold loan branches where our TAT would be maximum 30 minutes 
and within that all customization is being done. In gold loan portfolio, we are planning to add 
a good amount of business, not only in next quarter but also next year I can tell you. Another 
focus area is SHG. We are having tie-up arrangement with the 26 states NRLM and those are 
actually good opportunity to give great linkage to those SHG members that return is also very 
good in the SHG side and also there is very good opportunity to support these segments. In 
that way, the gold loan and SHGs are going to be the focus area. Apart from housing loan, 

 
 
Central Bank of India

our more than 50% advances under retail comes from housing loan. This is going to be the 
flag carrier now also. Car loan also, better dealer tie-up, both builder tie-up and car dealer tie-
up are going on. More and more CASA accounts, salary accounts, we are focusing upon in 
this quarter and actually, planning we have done for centering into the educational issues, the 
religious trusts, hospitals and other transport operators in a big way because we have 
established our marketing setup at different places. 300 marketing officers we have recruited 
in our bank, so with that workforce available and different products available for different 
segments of customers, those CASA customers will give an opportunity for particularly 
salary account customer, good opportunity for cross-selling of personal loan also. These are 
going to be our priority in next quarter. Thank you. 
Sushil Choksey: 
Sir, I would ask you if you could give me if there is an uptick in average ticket in gold loan 
not only because of price but the borrowing pattern and the same for housing loan and car 
loan because a lot of traditional Indians are moving from small cars to SUVs, the similar way 
gold prices have moved up and housing market is also 10% to 20% up on a national average 
basis, so is the number of loans increasing or the average ticket is increasing? 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Both I will give you one example, very recently in home loan, Rs.22 Crores green home loan 
we have provided and even ticket size is not a bar for us, no restrictions is there. Now, I can 
tell you, average ticket size is increasing day-by-day for housing loan and car loan also. So, 
depending upon our credit underwriting and utility of borrower, that is never a bar and 
naturally, we are more focusing on the good builder side where better ticket size is available, 
but as we are having our branches at rural semi-urban, where lower ticket sizes, up to Rs.30 
lakhs it is totally online process now and above Rs.30 lakhs, normal underwriting part is there 
and ticket size, as you are saying, that it is going to be our priority as we have geared up our 
CPAC also. We have revisited CPAC structure so that they are in a position to take even big 
ticket loan, not only in a housing loan or car loan processing, but also for MSME loan, 32 
places we have identified. Separate team managers are posted so that they can even 
underwrite the higher ticket size MSME loan also. It is both, I will say, numbers of customers 
and also ticket size wise also good number of customers will underwrite with the strength 
which Central Bank of India is having now. 
Sushil Choksey: 
Sir, two questions. How do you see CASA growing from here till March end and the deposit 
base? I know your guidance number would be 12% to 14%, 15% but strength of Central Bank 
has always been CASA. If you look historically over last 15 years or 10 years despite being 
in PCA that time also deposit was our strength and the franchisee is very strong in western 
region. How are we strengthening further cross-selling this CASA base? You said about 
salary accounts, but what other factors including digitization, digital apps, cross-selling, you 
have tied up with multiple insurance as well as mutual funds, you may be tying up for 

 
 
Central Bank of India 
October 19, 2026

brokerage houses, so to enhance Central Bank strength with certain multiple new ventures, 
and second, what is the corporate pipeline looking from now? I understand we are very good 
at RAM, but a balance of 65:32, 65:35, or 62:38 what area of business are we focusing on 
corporate book too and the third question would be your outlook on treasury? 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Yes, regarding CASA growth, rightly said by you, people love Central Bank of India, having 
115 years in service to the nation, therefore, it is being reflected in our CASA numbers also. 
I will give you one number. Our CASA has grown by 9.23%. We have crossed Rs.2,26,774 
Crores, growth of 9.23%. Savings deposit has grown by 9.32% and current account deposits 
also has grown with the kind of initiatives we have taken for CASA growth. As I told you, 
we have multiple customer acquisition centers and government business centers also we have 
opened. In that way, we are geared up to play whatever strength we are having. 
Geographically, you also told western side we have good presence, but we are having good 
presence in Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, and also Maharashtra side. These are the areas, Madhya 
Pradesh also we are having good number of branches and good presence, 2658 branches out 
of 4622 branches of Central Bank of India are having CASA percentage 50% and more. That 
is the strength Central Bank of India is deriving due to its geographical presence and the 
initiative which we have taken since last one year. Setting up of the customer acquisition 
centers, government business centers, placement of the 300 additional marketing officers, 
200 to 250 marketing officers were already there. This 500, 600 marketing team and now we 
have also started wealth management. It is just the beginning, and we have recruited some 
marketing officer at a wealth segment and we are going in a big way, from next January to 
June quarter, it may come in force fully, but now we have started, those things also will 
support our bank in not only mobilizing good CASA accounts, but also maintaining those 
CASA accounts with us. The CASA is the strength of this organization and with the initiatives 
which we have taken certainly it is going to continue. In June or so, we are going to start with 
our credit card franchise, which will support in mobilizing salary accounts and all. No doubt, 
if salary account increases then you have a good opportunity for cross-selling for all the retail 
products and also selling of other ancillary business and everything would be there. Cash 
management services also is going to be launched very soon. Two modules already launched, 
other modules in next few months we are going to launch that will support us in mobilizing 
current account from our corporates and also new customers. Regarding your second 
question, Corporate is approximately 7000 crores we are having undisbursed sanctions that 
we are having, and under process is 5000 Crores and under consideration, 11,000 crores. So 
corporate loan book, 24,000 loan book under consideration we are having. In the very near 
future, we are sure that we will get good traction in this corporate You see, previous year our 
corporate book was 83,000 Crores, this year it has grown by 44%, 1,18,666 Crores that is 
good growth and major area was actually roads, infrastructure, and also data center, 
technology side. All these things were our focus area, LRD. These were our focus area. Agri,

food processing, also some finances to NBFC, hospitality sector, so these were actually major 
area where we focused and in coming quarter also we are going to focus upon. Regarding 
treasury, as treasury yield is hardening. We ended by more than 7%, 7.19% yield during 
September 30, 2026 period. Now also it is progressing higher, 7.25%, 7.40%, so that actually, 
due to global turmoil and also rising interest rate scenario, rising inflation, and also having 
US rate of 5.35% plus that scenario actually does not bring comfort towards better treasury 
income. If you see our AFS, previous quarter from Rs.843 Crores to this quarter Rs.1023 
Crores there was a reduction. Mark-to-market challenge was there and in the coming scenario 
also, we are observing as yield is getting increased in that circumstances from treasury there 
are challenges. Though our treasury team has done a good job, they earned Rs.56 Crores by 
selling IPOs, by participating in IPOs and also, in the higher yield condition, the reinvestment 
side also, we will reinvest our maturing the securities and all to get better benefit. The outlook 
of treasury is the best opportunity. Market is not good you are aware because in AFS side, 
which is more exposed to market condition, is a challenge and it is, in my opinion, is going 
to continue in near future also, but building our portfolio judiciously and look not only driving 
the interest rate but also understanding properly and building our portfolio and reinvesting 
the things and the opportunity available within the law. I feel that treasury outlook would be 
challenged but it will contribute to the profitability as it has contributed this quarter also. 
Moderator: 
Thank you so much Sir. Mr. Choksey if you have any more questions you can rejoin the 
queue. We will take our next question now. We have Mr. Ashok Ajmera back in the queue 
here from Ajcon Global. Mr. Ajmera, please go ahead again. 
Ashok Ajmera: 
Sorry, Sir. There was some technical problem and I have missed some of your replies also. 
Can you hear me now? 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Yes, Ajmera Ji. You are always welcome. 
Ashok Ajmera: 
Sir, congratulations for a very good set of numbers and the Bank is really doing very well, 
even under your leadership also. Sir, going forward, like most of the questions, initially your 
address you have answered, but one is that on the ECL provisioning I might have missed your 
answer, that how prepared we are, what is the total quantum will be to be provided, can you 
give some color on that, Sir, some information? 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Yes, Ajmera ji. Actually, ECL provisioning, previous quarter also I told Rs.1525 Crores for 
Stage 1, Stage 2 we have provided till now and Stage 3 100% provision is there and Bank is 
prepared for meeting this requirement. Models are being prepared, data, quality, and all those 
aspects we are working and we expect that we have given guidance in this quarter, 
approximately Rs.5000 to Rs.5500 Crores may be required and with the kind of profit Central

Bank of India is garnering, we are sure that it is not going to be a challenge for Central Bank 
of India for meeting ECL requirement scheduled for implementation from April 1, 2027. 
Ashok Ajmera: 
Point well taken Sir. Sir, we are doing very well in the retail side of the loans even our home 
loan rates are also very, very competitive, going forward I might have missed your answer 
what is the plan of increasing the corporate book and where do we stand and what is the 
average yield now we are expecting from the corporate book and what is the sanction pipeline 
and the proposals which are in pipeline? 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Previous year if you see our corporate book in September 2025 was Rs.83,000 Crores and 
this September 2026 we have closed at Rs.1,18,666 Crores with a growth of 42% and out of 
total book 32% comes from this corporate side. There is increase year-on-year, which is 42% 
in corporate book size and actually, regarding pipeline, pending disbursement is Rs.7000 plus 
Crores and a proposal of Rs.5200 plus Crores is under process and Rs.11,000 Crores are under 
consideration. They may come in the NBG and all. Approximately Rs.24,000 Crores, 
corporate loan book, at present, we are actually having. So we will have good growth in 
corporate side. Regarding the credit yield, this year, overall, average yield was 7.87% on 
advances. Major areas that we are focusing upon, is renewable energy, roads, and also data 
center, some exposure in real estate, hospitality, and manufacturing segment, NBFC, agri-
food processing, logistic side, these are the major areas where actually we are focusing upon 
in this quarter and coming quarter. 
Ashok Ajmera: 
Very good, sir. Coming to the recoveries, recovery from the written off book has been decent. 
So going forward, what do we expect? We expect some more major bounty from this. What 
is our total written-off book balance outstanding and how much we expect on an average in 
percentage terms? Secondary on the recovery is, that old aviation account, so what is the 
status there, are that additional collateral which we had of 1200 Crores or 1500 Crores odd, 
whether that has been realized and how much recovery has already taken place and how much 
more we do expect to recover from that account sir? 
Kalyan Kumar: 
See, recovery in written off was Rs.485 Crores in this quarter good number we have got. If I 
talk about the pool, it is Rs.31,301 Crores. We are having ample pool now also written off 
accounts from where we can actually recover good significant amount. Previous year you 
have seen more than 2,000 to 2,700 Crores we have recovered for the full year. This year also 
I find sufficient ground and sufficient resources available to recover 2,500 plus Crores in this 
segment. Regarding answering your aviation sector account, recovery is expected of Rs.700 
Crores through SARFAESI and the auction process is going on, and we have got bidder also. 
We may get Rs.700 Crores in this aviation account in this current quarter or next quarter. 
There are some big accounts, and smaller accounts also, from where we will improve our

recovery numbers. I can assure you that kind of book and things available with us recovery 
numbers are going to be better than what we have done in this quarter. I am fully confident 
about that. 
Ashok Ajmera: 
Very good, sir. On the recovery for the small account under the OTS, how are we framing 
our policies and are we liberal to get at least those accounts where 100% provision has already 
been made and the securities are minimal? What is our emphasis of recovering on those small

Kalyan Kumar: 
Thank you Ajmera ji for asking this question. See, smaller accounts for that special OTS 
scheme we have got approved from our Board and it is very transparent process. We are 
coming with this technological capability, we call it E-OTS and here aid of NPA and 
availability of security and provision. These are the logic to which system itself derives that 
this amount if you pay, OTS would be done through digital process and branch assisted 
process, this we are going to implement very soon. There is another scheme which is called 
Kisan Rin Mochan scheme. Through BCA scheme, small value accounts, we are recovering 
a good amount in a very transparent manner. And you are right, because we deal with retail 
business. Put a number under slippage, under Rs.10 lakh segment. There are all these major 
electronic OTS, and this Kisan Rin Mochan scheme through BC agents and all these things 
are going to be very effective tool and support us in recovering the desired amount as per 
regulatory guidelines and cleaning up our books. So, our focus is also there and auctioning 
the property available for collateral security are there. I am giving you one example. Previous 
year, total auction of properties was 485. This half year we reached that number. Very 
effective monitoring of SARFAESI process is also actually bringing both customers on the 
negotiation table, through OTS mode also. we are recovering significant amount and closing 
those accounts through OTS also. That way I can tell you from recovery side, the asset quality 
which we are observing 2.39 and 0.31 net NPA, it is going to be continuously, you will find 
improvement in these numbers in coming days.

Thank you so much, sir. Mr. Ajmera, if you have any more questions, you can rejoin the 
queue. You can click on the raise hand icon again if you wish to ask a question. We will move 
to our next participant. Before that reminding all the participants, if you have any questions, 
please click on the raise hand icon from the participants tab on your screen. We are taking

Thank you, sir. Good morning, Mr. Kalyan. 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Good morning.

Rajesh Agarwal: 
From the last few quarters, we have been tracking Central Bank and let me congratulate you 
for the kind of numbers that you have given in the last quarter and followed by this quarter. 
It was really good, I would say. And I would say we are very satisfied with the kind of 
numbers because we have recommended to so many of our clients. There was just one query 
which I would like to have a clarification like reported gross NPA, net NPA, slippages, they 
all improved, yet provisions went up. Can you throw some light on the breakdown of the 
provisioning, whether into standard assets or floating or technical? Why this specific 
provisions went up and which segment, maybe specifically retail, MSME or unsecured loan, 
where the reasons for this higher provision? And the last one would be, what is your credit 
cost guidance for FY2027? 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Yes, thank you Rajesh Agarwal ji for your good words for Central Bank of India. You are 
right, our gross NPA, net NPA, and slippage ratio are under control and provisions have 
increased actually and credit cost also, you see, 0.53% in this quarter. Though they are well 
within, because credit costs we have given guidance of that need to remain up to 0.75%, it is 
0.53%, and PCR is 97.16%, that is also well within our guidance given to the market. But 
reason, what you have asked, actually you know, we must build enough provision in good 
times for facing any challenges or anything which may come in future. It is very resilient and 
I will say the resilient approach which Bank has taken. And for that purpose, you must have 
been observing that our provision coverage ratio has increased since last quarter. That is the 
main reason. Otherwise, another one important reason, our standard advances also have 
grown significantly because previous year, September 2025, Provision on Standard Advances 
was 30 or 37, now it is 399. That increase is there. So these are the reason behind increase in 
credit cost side. Hope I have answered your question Rajesh Agarwal ji. 
Rajesh Agarwal: 
Thank you sir. Thank you so much and best wishes for future  quarters too. Thank you so 
much sir. 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Thank you. 
Moderator: 
Thank you Mr. Agarwal. Requesting participants to please click on the raise hand icon from 
the participants tab on your screen. We will take our next question. We have Mr. Ashlesh 
Sonje of Kotak Securities. Please unmute your microphone, Mr. Sonje. Yes, please go ahead. 
Ashlesh Sonje: 
Hi, team. Good morning. Sir, few questions from my side. Firstly, on the ECL, you have 
reported a credit cost of roughly 50-basis points in this quarter. Do you have a sense of how 
much your credit cost will be next year after you have transitioned to the ECL regime? 
Kalyan Kumar: 
Yes, Ashlesh, thanks for this question. Actually ECL, we are preparing, I understand. The 
banks which are having better credit underwriting would have better control over the credit

cost. And this year credit cost 0.53 is actually, you must have observed, the answer which I 
have just now given to Rajesh Agarwal ji. We have just to give you comfort and make you 
understand in a better way how Central Bank of India is prepared or preparing itself to face 
the consequences of implementation of ECL, that will give you answer. March 2025, our 
slippage ratio was 1.47, March 2026 is came down to 1.16. And this quarter, it is 0.24. And
